test_title: PYST 25: Selection Post (Matric Level) - General Intelligence (Held On 30 Jun 2023 Shift 3)
subject: reasoning
question:
Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

All trucks are buses.

Some buses are bikes.

All bikes are planes.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some planes are buses.

II. Some buses are trucks.

III. All planes are trucks.

options.text: Only conclusions I and III follow
Only conclusions II and III follow
Only conclusions I and II follow

solution:
Given statements: 

All trucks are buses. 

Some buses are bikes. 

All bikes are planes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8b6c873a71f37bb7a98319c45c46eb40397907865cb479a27eebee5b92642270.png] 

**Conclusions**:

I. Some planes are buses - **True **(Because, those part of planes which is bikes will buses also)

II. Some buses are trucks - **True **(Because, All trucks are buses implies that some buses are trucks)

III. All planes are trucks - False (Because, there is no definite relation given between planes and trucks, so it can be possible only)

Thus, Only Conclusions I and II follow.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 4".**
